item.title: Measuring and improving the quality of my notes
item.author: emecas
item.description: This blog started as a text file. For more than ten years I kept short notes in one file, Index.txt, in a Git repository: a title, a link, sometimes a line or two about why it mattered. Later came notes from the repositories I star on GitHub, from issues I open as reminders, and from articles. Today there are 1,432 of them on this site, and more are coming: I have more than 20 other data sources still to process and include, such as bookmarks, podcast notes, notes on my favorite blogs and the books I read.

item.title: Universal Tool Calling Protocol (UTCP)
item.author: emecas
item.description:
Universal Tool Calling Protocol (UTCP)
Universal Tool Calling Protocol (UTCP)
https://www.utcp.io/

Spec: https://github.com/universal-tool-calling-protocol/utcp-specification ★ star note

Version: 1.1
Universal Tool Calling Protocol (UTCP)
Language Examples

UTCP is available in multiple languages - see Python: https://github.com/universal-tool-calling-protocol/python-utcp, TypeScript: https://github.com/universal-tool-calling-protocol/typescript-utcp, Go: https://github.com/universal-tool-calling-protocol/go-utcp, and other implementations in the UTCP GitHub organization: https://github.com/universal-tool-calling-protocol.

UTCP is a lightweight, secure, and scalable standard that enables AI agents and applications to discover and call tools directly using their native protocols - no wrapper servers required.

item.title: Kiri : A Docker Desktop Replacement in Rust That Starts Containers in 2.5 Milliseconds
item.author: emecas
item.description:
Kiri : A Docker Desktop Replacement in Rust That Starts Containers in 2.5 Milliseconds
Project Description

View on GitHub: https://github.com/libracoder/kiri?utm_source=opensourceprojects.dev&ref=opensourceprojects.dev ★ star note

A Docker Desktop Replacement in Rust That Starts Containers in 2.5 Milliseconds

If you’ve ever waited for Docker Desktop to wake up, spin up its VM, and finally get around to running your container, you know the feeling. You open a terminal, type

docker run

, and then sit there while your machine thinks about it. Kiri is a bet that this doesn’t have to be how it works—it’s a lightweight container runtime written in Rust that aims to replace Docker Desktop and OrbStack without the weight.
